questions.q: What single requirement drives the batch vs. streaming choice more than any other?
options: The programming language the team prefers
Freshness — how quickly the data needs to be usable after it's produced
The total number of engineers on the team
Whether the data is stored as CSV or Parquet
questions.explain: "Update once a night is fine" points to batch; "needs to be seen within seconds" points to streaming.

questions.q: Why is choosing streaming when batch would satisfy the requirement a mistake, not a sign of sophistication?
options: Batch systems are incapable of handling any real workload
This is actually the correct default choice in all situations
Streaming costs more to build, run, and operate correctly, so choosing it unnecessarily is needless cost and complexity for no real benefit
Streaming is always technically inferior to batch in every case
questions.explain: Fabric Lesson 54's cost management lesson made this explicit — windowing, watermarks, and production practices exist because streaming makes things genuinely harder.

questions.q: What is a hybrid processing model, according to this lesson?
options: A single tool that automatically switches between batch and streaming
A compromise where neither streaming nor batch actually works correctly
Using streaming for everything, just with a cheaper Fabric Capacity SKU
Running a fast streaming hot path for freshness alongside a slower, thoroughly-correct batch cold path for historical accuracy
questions.explain: This isn't indecision — it's matching each requirement to the tool that actually fits it.

questions.q: How does this lesson's hybrid decision relate to Lesson 4's storage choice?
options: Lesson 4's principle only applies to storage and has no broader application
Processing model choice and storage choice are completely unrelated decisions
Hybrid processing always requires OLTP storage specifically
It applies the same principle — matching each requirement to the right tool — to processing instead of storage
questions.explain: Just as a platform can use OLTP, OLAP, and object storage for different parts, it can use streaming and batch for different parts.

questions.q: According to this lesson's decision framework, when does batch remain the right choice?
options: Batch is never actually the right choice in a modern data platform
Only when a Fabric Capacity SKU is unavailable
Only when the data volume is too small for any streaming tool to handle
When nightly or hourly updates are genuinely fine, and the simplicity of batch has real value
questions.explain: This choice should follow directly from the actual freshness requirement, not a default preference for either option.
